AI-Powered Intelligent VPN & Connectivity Platform

A smarter and safer approach to managing VPN connectivity

Presented by Elijah Fullah
Good morning/afternoon everyone. Today I’m presenting DēGlitch, an AI-powered intelligent VPN and connectivity management platform. The idea behind this system came from a personal problem I experienced when I arrived in a new country.

    The problem I experienced

    I arrived in a new country and needed access to the applications and online services I was used to.

    I downloaded multiple VPN applications, looking for something that worked.

    But I didn’t know which VPN applications I could trust.

    Which of these can I trust?
    When I arrived, I was very eager to continue using the applications and services I was accustomed to. Because I needed a VPN, I started downloading different VPN applications. The problem was that I was mainly focused on finding something that worked. I wasn’t paying enough attention to whether the applications themselves were trustworthy.     The problem is bigger than one user

    Untrusted VPN apps

    Users may download apps without knowing:

    • Who operates them
    • How they handle data
    • Whether the app is trustworthy
    • What permissions it needs

    Manual server choice

    Singapore?Japan?Hong Kong?US?UK?

    …without understanding which server is actually appropriate.

    Changing conditions

    A server that works well now may become congested later.

    Good connection
    Server becomes busy
    Latency increases
    Packet loss increases
    Poor experience

    Blind to your activity

    Gaming, video calls, streaming and software development need different things from a network.

    No visible cause

    VPN connected.

    …but they still see:

    • Slow connection
    • High latency
    • Packet loss
    • Unstable connection
    Now move from your personal story to the general problem. Five challenges: untrusted apps, manual server choice, conditions that change, apps that don’t understand what the user is doing, and users who can’t tell why a connection is bad — they simply see "VPN connected."

    What if a VPN could think about the connection instead of simply connecting?

    This led me to the idea behind DēGlitch. Instead of building another application where the user simply chooses a server and connects, what if the system could actually understand the user’s needs, analyze the network, evaluate available servers and recommend the most appropriate option?

    Introducing DēGlitch

    An AI-powered intelligent VPN and connectivity management platform that analyzes user requirements, network conditions and server performance to provide intelligent connection recommendations.

    Understand

    • The user
    • The network
    • Available servers

    Decide

    • Uses a custom ML model
    • Ranks servers
    • Recommends a server

    Manage

    • Manages the VPN connection
    • Monitors the connection
    • Alerts the user
    Walk left to right. DēGlitch understands the user, the network and the available servers; it decides using a custom ML model that ranks servers and recommends one; then it manages the VPN connection, monitors it and alerts the user.

    The same server isn’t necessarily ideal for every activity. A gamer may care more about latency, while someone watching high-resolution video may care more about bandwidth. DēGlitch takes the user’s activity into consideration when generating its recommendation.

    DēGlitch doesn’t simply connect and forget about the connection. It continuously monitors it so the system can understand whether the connection remains healthy.     Problem solved

    The user doesn’t need to understand networking to troubleshoot basic connection problems.

    When something goes wrong, the user can ask "Why is my connection slow?" and DēGlitch investigates: latency, packet loss, DNS, the VPN endpoint and server load, then returns a diagnosis with a recommendation.

    Predictive connection and failover

    Predictive connection

    The model learns these patterns from historical data and can recognize that a server frequently degrades under similar conditions.

    It estimates expected performance; it doesn’t claim to predict the future perfectly.

    Intelligent failover

    Current server
    Connection deteriorates
    Network monitoring detects the problem
    AI re-evaluates the servers
    Alternative server identified
    VPN management handles the reconnection
    Singapore-03 unstableAlternative available

    Starts as recommendation-based failover; switching depends on user settings.

    Predictive: the system doesn’t claim to predict the future perfectly. The machine-learning model learns patterns from historical network and server data and uses them to estimate expected performance. Failover: the system can recommend or, depending on your final implementation and user settings, initiate a switch to an authorized alternative. For the academic implementation, start with recommendation-based failover rather than promising fully automatic switching.

    Instead of relying entirely on an external AI API, DēGlitch will use a custom machine-learning model trained for server-performance prediction and recommendation. Inputs: latency, packet loss, jitter, server load, bandwidth, availability, historical performance and user activity. Outputs: a server score and a performance prediction, which the ranking algorithm turns into a recommendation.

    Why build our own model?

    Specialized

    The model is designed specifically for our problem.

    More control

    We control the training data and the model’s behavior.

    No external AI API

    The core recommendation system doesn’t have to depend on Gemini or OpenAI.

    Privacy

    Network telemetry can stay inside our own architecture instead of going to a general-purpose AI provider.

    Software engineering value

    It demonstrates the full lifecycle:

    Data collectionData processingMachine learningModel trainingModel evaluationAPI and backend integrationApplication integration
    Five reasons: it is specialized, gives us more control, removes the dependency on an external AI API, protects privacy, and demonstrates real software engineering value — data collection, processing, machine learning, training, evaluation, and backend and application integration. That makes the project substantially more interesting academically.

    How the AI learns

    Not magic. It is a proper data pipeline, from history to a trained model.

    Historical network data
    Data cleaning
    Feature engineering
    Training dataset
    Model training
    Model evaluation
    Trained model
    DēGlitch
    A historical recordWhat the model learns to connect
    Latency45 ms
    Packet loss0.2%
    Jitter5 ms
    Load32%
    ActivityGaming
    Connection qualityGood

    The model learns the relationships between these features and connection outcomes.

    Don’t say "we put data into AI and it magically learns." Explain it properly: historical network data is cleaned, features are engineered, a training dataset is built, the model is trained and evaluated, and the trained model is integrated into DēGlitch. For example, a record with 45 ms latency, 0.2% packet loss, 5 ms jitter, 32% load and Gaming activity is labelled as good connection quality.

    DēGlitch architecture

    The loop never stops

    Metrics feed the model. Recommendations flow back into VPN management. Monitoring continues after the connection is made.

    You’ve explained the why and what; now explain the how. The user goes through User Management to VPN Management, which talks to the VPN and network infrastructure. Metrics flow to the Network Monitor, then to the AI/ML Engine with the custom model, and the recommendation returns to VPN Management. Then introduce the DFD levels.

    What makes DēGlitch different?

    Intelligent server selectionIt doesn’t just list servers. It analyzes them.
    Activity-aware recommendationsGaming isn’t treated like streaming or video calling.
    Continuous network awarenessIt keeps evaluating the connection after connecting.
    Custom machine learningThe core model is built specifically for DēGlitch.
    Explainable recommendationsIt can explain why a server was recommended.
    Integrated diagnosticsIt doesn’t only connect. It investigates problems.
    Multilingual designEnglish, Chinese, Spanish, French, Russian and Krio.

    One integrated platform: DēGlitch brings these together.

    Don’t simply say "DēGlitch is unique because it uses AI" — that’s too weak. Point to the specifics: it analyzes servers rather than listing them, it is activity-aware, it stays aware of the network after connecting, its core model is custom, its recommendations are explainable, diagnostics are built in, and the interface is multilingual. Finally, instead of a VPN app plus a speed test plus a network diagnostic app plus a server selector plus a notification system, DēGlitch brings these together in one platform.

    Security is treated as a core design requirement throughout the system.

    Secure authentication

    Encrypted communication

    Secure storage of credentials

    Minimal permissions

    Trusted, authorized VPN infrastructure

    Secure API communication

    Because the project originated from a security incident, this slide matters. Don’t claim "DēGlitch is completely secure." Say: security is treated as a core design requirement throughout the system. That’s much more defensible.
